---
title: "Session 2: Reproducible Actuarial Analysis with R"
---

## Theme

Turning validated data into actuarial insight.

This session teaches the middle of the mini-project workflow: joining valid claims to policies, creating derived actuarial measures, and producing summaries that another actuary can check.

## Learning Outcomes

At the end of this session, participants will be able to:

- Build a reproducible actuarial workflow in R.
- Create derived variables and actuarial summary measures.
- Write reusable functions for repetitive tasks.
- Perform grouped summaries and simple statistical analyses.
- Organise code for readability, reuse, and reproducibility.
- Document assumptions and intermediate results within a Quarto notebook.

## Case Study Milestone

Participants reproduce Sections 3 and 4 of the mini-project:

- Exclude unmatched claims from portfolio metrics after documenting them.
- Summarise claims at policy level.
- Join claim totals to policy records.
- Create age bands and risk bands.
- Calculate claim frequency, average severity, pure premium, and loss ratio.
- Summarise results by product, region, age band, and risk band.

## Suggested Timing

| Time | Activity |
|---:|---|
| 15 min | Review data checks from Session 1 |
| 30 min | Join policy and claims data |
| 30 min | Create derived actuarial measures |
| 25 min | Summarise by segment and risk profile |
| 15 min | AI-assisted code review |
| 5 min | Wrap-up |

## Core Code From The Mini-Project

```{r}
#| eval: false

# Keep only claims linked to known policies.
valid_claims <- claims |>
  semi_join(policies, by = "policy_id")

# Summarise claims by policy before joining.
claims_by_policy <- valid_claims |>
  group_by(policy_id) |>
  summarise(
    claim_count = n(),
    claim_amount = sum(claim_amount, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Join policies to their claim totals.
portfolio <- policies |>
  left_join(claims_by_policy, by = "policy_id") |>
  mutate(
    claim_count = if_else(is.na(claim_count), 0L, claim_count),
    claim_amount = if_else(is.na(claim_amount), 0, claim_amount),
    claim_frequency = claim_count / exposure,
    average_severity = if_else(claim_count > 0, claim_amount / claim_count, 0),
    pure_premium = claim_amount / exposure,
    loss_ratio = claim_amount / earned_premium
  )
```

## AI Checkpoint

Use AI to review the code structure and identify possible errors. Then verify the output yourself by checking row counts, totals, and whether policies with no claims are handled correctly.
